skill.name: writing-plans
skill.description: Creates detailed, test-first implementation plans before code changes begin.
skill.summary: Turns requirements into step-by-step implementation plans with files, tests, commands, and handoff options.
skill.author: Cygnusfear

security_audit.summary: All 16 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code or fenced examples in SKILL.md. The skill describes how to write implementation plans and does not include executable scripts, dynamic shell execution, network access, or credential access. No semantic evidence of data exfiltration or malicious prompt injection was found.

content.value_statement: Teams often start complex coding work without enough structure. This skill turns requirements into clear plans with files, tests, commands, and handoff steps.
actual_capabilities: Creates implementation plans from requirements before code changes begin.
Breaks work into small tasks with test, implementation, verification, and commit steps.
Includes exact file paths, expected tests, and example commands in generated plans.
Uses a standard plan header with goal, architecture, and technology stack sections.
Provides execution handoff options after saving the plan.
limitations: Does not implement code changes by itself.
Needs clear requirements or a specification to produce useful plans.
May reference companion skills that must exist in the user's environment.
Generated commands should be reviewed before execution.

use_cases.title: Plan a Feature Before Coding
use_cases.description: Turn a feature request into a test-first implementation plan before editing files.

use_cases.title: Prepare Team Implementation Notes
use_cases.description: Create a shared plan that names affected files, expected tests, and review checkpoints.

use_cases.title: Create an AI Coding Handoff
use_cases.description: Prepare a handoff plan for Claude, Codex, or Claude Code before a separate implementation session.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Small Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use writing-plans for this requirement: [paste requirement]. Create a short test-first plan with exact files and commands.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a small code change

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Use writing-plans to create an implementation plan for [feature]. Include tasks, tests, expected failures, and commit points.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Safe Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Use writing-plans for this refactor: [scope]. Preserve behavior, identify regression tests, and split the work into small commits.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Multi-Service Rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Use writing-plans for this cross-system change: [spec]. Include dependencies, migration order, rollback checks, and verification commands.

output_examples.input: A request to add validation to an API endpoint.
output: Plan header with goal, architecture, and stack.
Tasks for failing tests, minimal implementation, passing tests, and commit.
Exact file paths and verification commands for each task.

output_examples.input: A request to refactor a shared module without behavior changes.
output: Plan separates characterization tests from implementation.
Each task names files to modify and tests to run.
The handoff section asks how execution should proceed.

output_examples.input: A request to implement a data migration.
output_examples.output: A staged plan with migration checks, rollback notes, focused tests, and final verification steps.

best_practices: Provide the current spec, target files, and known constraints before invoking the skill.
Ask for focused tasks that fit one small test or implementation step.
Review generated commands before running them in a real repository.
anti_patterns: Using the skill when the requirement is vague or missing acceptance criteria.
Treating generated commands as approved automation without review.
Skipping tests because the plan already describes the intended behavior.

faq.question: Does this skill write code for me?
faq.answer: No. It creates implementation plans before code changes begin.

faq.question: Where does it save plans?
faq.answer: It instructs the assistant to save plans under docs/plans with a date and feature name.

faq.question: Can it work with Codex and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Does it run shell commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill contains example commands for generated plans, but it does not execute commands itself.

faq.question: What input should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the requirement, important constraints, target areas, and test expectations.

faq.question: What should I review before using a plan?
faq.answer: Check file paths, commands, dependencies, and any referenced companion skills.
